newsitems.title: PAS1 Finals 2 Day 3
newsitems.author: JBowlerr
newsitems.contents: [p]The last weekend of PAS1 is just around the corner, and there’s plenty to catch up on. From how things have unfolded so far to what’s on the line, plus Twitch drops, format details, and the full schedule, here’s your complete rundown.[/p][h3][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260506/qUILtINr.png"][/img][/h3][p align="start"]PAS1 introduced an exciting new format this season, featuring two separate rounds of Playoffs and Finals. We’ve already seen Playoffs 1 and Finals 1 wrap up, with Team Falcons claiming the top spot, closely followed by Godlike and Team Liquid. After that, everything was reset, and the competition kicked off again with Playoffs 2 last weekend. From there, 16 teams secured their place in this weekend’s Finals 2. Here’s who made the cut:[/p][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260506/fL46qDHs.png"][/img][/p][h3][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260506/kgsiHf4i.png"][/img][/h3][p align="start"]It’s not just the players walking away with rewards this weekend. Viewers can also earn in-game items simply by tuning into the PAS1 Finals on Twitch. These drops will also be available during the PUBG EMEA Championship broadcasts.[/p][p align="start"][b]May 8[/b][/p][list][*][p]Watch 60 minutes of the stream: Friendly Fire (Spray)[/p][/*][*][p]Watch 120 minutes of the stream: Networked Gloves[/p][/*][/list][p align="start"][/p][p align="start"][b]May 9[/b][/p][list][*][p]Watch 60 minutes of the stream: Victory Dance 142[/p][/*][*][p]Watch 120 minutes of the stream: Foulmouthed Mask[/p][/*][/list][p align="start"][/p][p align="start"][b]May 10[/b][/p][list][*][p]Watch 30 minutes of the stream: Lipovka Slacks[/p][/*][*][p]Watch 60 minutes of the stream: Dash Doberman Tee[/p][/*][*][p]Watch 120 minutes of the stream: Serpent’s Garden Jacket[/p][/*][/list][p align="start"][/p][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260506/xRtZBhrM.jpg"][/img][/p][p align="start"][/p][p align="start"]Drops will be active on [u][url="https://www.twitch.tv/pubg_battlegrounds"]PUBG: Battlegrounds (EN)[/url][/u], [u][url="https://www.twitch.tv/pubg_br"]PUBG: Battlegrounds (PTBR)[/url][/u][/p][p align="start"][/p][h3]What’s the format?[/h3][p align="start"]The format for the Finals remains a familiar one. Sixteen teams will battle it out across three days, playing a total of 15 matches. By the end of Sunday, the team with the highest overall points will be crowned the Finals 2 Champion. [/p][h3]What’s at stake?[/h3][p align="start"]These Finals are a major proving ground for teams looking to make it onto the global stage. Most importantly, this is where the majority of PGC Points are up for grabs, the key factor in qualifying for the PUBG Global Championship, the pinnacle event in PUBG Esports. While some points were earned during the Playoffs, the Finals carry much greater weight, making them the decisive stage in the qualification race.[/p][p align="start"]There’s even more on the line, too. The two teams with the highest total PGC Points from PEC: Spring will earn direct qualification to the Esports World Cup in Riyadh later this year, along with entry into all PUBG Global Series events in the second half of the season, including PGS Circuits 3 and 4.[/p][p align="start"]And to top it all off, each Finals weekend features a $30,000 prize pool, giving every team even more incentive to perform when it matters most.[/p][p align="start"][/p][p align="start"]Be sure to tune in on our [u][url="https://www.twitch.tv/pubg_battlegrounds"]Twitch[/url][/u], [u][url="https://www.youtube.com/@PUBGEsports"]YouTube[/url][/u] and [u][url="https://kick.com/pubgesports"]Kick[/url][/u] channels to catch all of the action![/p]

newsitems.title: PEC: Spring Finals 2 - Day 3
newsitems.author: JBowlerr
newsitems.contents: [p]It’s almost time for the final weekend of PEC: Spring! Here’s everything you need to know about the story so far, what’s at stake, Twitch drops, format, schedule and more.[/p][h3][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260506/SoxXlnlY.jpg"][/img][/h3][p align="start"]PEC: Spring features a new double-trouble format, with two sets of Playoffs and Finals! We’ve already seen the conclusion of Playoffs 1 and Finals 1 - where Virtus.pro took the throne (with Twisted Minds and Team Nemesis following closely behind). Afterwards, we wiped the slate clean and started from scratch again with Playoffs 2 last weekend - which saw 16 teams qualify to this weekend’s upcoming [b]Finals 2.[/b] Here’s the full list of teams:[/p][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260506/GUvo3EBd.png"][/img][/p][p align="start"][/p][h3][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260506/np2i3Sji.jpg"][/img][/h3][p align="start"]The pro players won’t be the only ones who’ll be earning a prize this weekend - you can also score some in-game items just by watching the PEC: Spring Finals on Twitch! (if you miss the PEC stream, you can also snag these during the PUBG Americas Series streams, which take place about an hour or two after PEC finishes each day)[/p][p align="start"][/p][p align="start"][b]May 8[/b][/p][list][*][p]Watch 60 minutes of the stream: Friendly Fire (Spray)[/p][/*][*][p]Watch 120 minutes of the stream: Networked Gloves[/p][/*][/list][p align="start"][/p][p align="start"][b]May 9[/b][/p][list][*][p]Watch 60 minutes of the stream: Victory Dance 142[/p][/*][*][p]Watch 120 minutes of the stream: Foulmouthed Mask[/p][/*][/list][p align="start"][/p][p align="start"][b]May 10[/b][/p][list][*][p]Watch 30 minutes of the stream: Lipovka Slacks[/p][/*][*][p]Watch 60 minutes of the stream: Dash Doberman Tee[/p][/*][*][p]Watch 120 minutes of the stream: Serpent’s Garden Jacket[/p][/*][/list][p align="start"][/p][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260506/VEbVp3iF.jpg"][/img][/p][p align="start"][/p][p align="start"]Drops will be active on [u][url="https://www.twitch.tv/pubg_battlegrounds"]PUBG: Battlegrounds (EN)[/url][/u], [u][url="https://www.twitch.tv/pubg_battlegroundstr"]PUBG: Battlegrounds (TR)[/url][/u], [u][url="https://www.twitch.tv/pubg_cis"]PUBG: Battlegrounds (CIS[/url][/u]).[/p][p align="start"][/p][h3]What’s the format?[/h3][p align="start"]The PEC: Spring Finals format is tried and tested - 16 teams will face off over three days, for a total of 15 matches. Whoever has the most points at the end of play on Sunday will be crowned the Finals 2 Champion! [/p][p align="start"][/p][p align="center"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260506/byfggjV0.png"][/img][/p][p align="start"][/p][h3]What’s at stake?[/h3][p align="start"]The PEC: Spring Finals are a crucial battleground for any team aiming to compete on the global stage. Most importantly, the Finals are where the bulk of PGC Points are earned, the key metric used to qualify for the crown jewel of the PUBG Esports calendar, the PUBG Global Championship. While teams had a chance to collect some points during the Playoffs, the Finals offer significantly more, making them the defining moment in the race for qualification.[/p][p align="start"]Beyond that, the stakes extend even further. The top two teams with the highest cumulative PGC Points from PEC: Spring will secure direct qualification to the Esports World Cup in Riyadh later this year, as well as all PUBG Global Series events in the second half of the season (meaning PGS Circuit 3 and 4).[/p][p align="start"][/p][p align="start"]And if that wasn’t enough, each Finals weekend also features a $30,000 prize pool, giving teams yet another reason to bring their best when it matters most.[/p][p align="start"][/p][p align="start"]Be sure to tune in on our [u][url="https://www.twitch.tv/pubg_battlegrounds"]Twitch[/url][/u], [u][url="https://www.youtube.com/@PUBGEsports"]YouTube[/url][/u] and [u][url="https://kick.com/pubgesports"]Kick[/url][/u] channels to catch all of the action![/p]

newsitems.title: PUBG Global Series Circuit 2 is about to drop!
newsitems.author: Eoin
newsitems.contents:
[p]A little over a month after Circuit 1's unpredictable three weeks, the 24 teams are back in Seoul. The PUBG Global Series returns with its second circuit — PGS 4-6 — kicking off May 20.[/p][p align="start"]Circuit 2 isn't a reset. The PGS Points earned in Circuit 1 carry directly into the standings, and the final results here decide who qualifies for the Esports World Cup (EWC). Add a new patch to the mix, and the question becomes: how do the strategies teams locked in during Circuit 1 hold up in a different environment?[/p][p align="start"] [/p][h2]Circuit 2 Overview[/h2][p align="start"] [/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27971017/6211a4eea73f9b192067303cc970e33c5944d8ff.png"][/img][/p][list][*][p]Location: Seongsu, Seoul, South Korea[/p][/*][*][p]Participating Teams: 24 Teams[/p][/*][*][p]Total Prize Pool: $500,000 (PGS 4-5: $100,000 each / PGS 6: $300,000)[/p][/*][/list][p align="start"]All Circuit 2 matches begin at 19:00 KST (10:00 UTC / 11:00 CET / 17:00 ICT / 03:00 PDT) daily. 
[i]*PGS 4 Day 1 Group Stage begins at 14:00 KST (05:00 UTC / 06:00 CET / 12:00 ICT / 22:00 PDT†). † Previous day (May 19)[/i][/p][p align="start"] [/p][h3]Group Stage Seeding — Based on PGS 3 Results[/h3][p align="start"]Circuit 2 Group Stage seeding was drawn via snake draft from PGS 3 final standings. Circuit 1 results shape the starting line of Circuit 2 directly.[/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27971017/31b424e473be85946f59751252a640ea40f5d272.png"][/img][/p][p align="start"] [/p][h2]Looking Back at Circuit 1 — The Starting Point of Circuit 2[/h2][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27971017/4d6a26eb82b7b2626def67d8845c9bbb33a869bf.png"][/img][/p][p align="start"]These are the top 12 teams in PGS Points from Circuit 1 — the teams closest to the EWC qualification line heading into Circuit 2. Their performance over the next three weeks will decide who makes the cut: the top 8 teams in cumulative first-half PGS Points earn EWC spots.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][h2]What's Changed from Circuit 1 — Game Updates[/h2][p align="start"]The biggest variable in Circuit 2 is the game patch. PGS 4 and PGS 5 run on the April Update (Patch 41.1), which brings several updates that could directly affect team strategy. How Circuit 1's refined approaches hold up in this new environment is the circuit's biggest storyline.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][h3]Terrain Destruction Reshapes the Battlefield[/h3][p align="start"]The headline change is a major expansion of terrain destruction.[/p][p align="start"]Erangel now joins Rondo, Taego, Sanhok, and Miramar — meaning terrain itself becomes a tactical layer across all major competitive maps. Pickaxe strikes also dig deeper than before, giving teams new options for cover and route design.[/p][p align="start"]Terrain is no longer a fixed environment, but something players can shape. How new combat patterns emerge through grenades, mortars, Panzerfausts, C4, pickaxes, and vehicle explosions will be a key watchpoint throughout Circuit 2.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][h3]Gunplay — New Options and Rebalanced Weapons[/h3][p align="start"]The most notable gunplay change in this patch is the new Hybrid Scope.[/p][p align="start"]The Hybrid Scope switches between 1x and 4x magnification instantly, covering both close- and mid-range fights with a single attachment. It fills the void left by the Canted Sight's removal and should reshape how pros approach attachment choices and engagement distance.[/p][p align="start"]The patch also includes additional new attachments and weapon balancing. Grip-tier changes and recoil adjustments to key weapons are in, so expect teams to revisit their gun setups and combat approach.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][h3]Gameplay — New Variables for Supply and Survival[/h3][p align="start"]This patch introduces a new support item (the Emergency Support Flare), expanded Trigger Backpack tiers, and new BlueChip Tower functionality.[/p][p align="start"]The BlueChip Tower changes stand out. Destroying enemy BlueChips to block revives used to be the whole play — now, teams can spend 2 enemy BlueChips at a BlueChip Tower to call in an air supply drop. Enemy BlueChips become a resource instead of just something to remove, and Circuit 2 should showcase far more strategic usage around them.[/p][p align="start"]Circuit 2's final series, PGS 6, runs on a version that incorporates the May Update. Details will follow in the May Patch Notes.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][h2]Map Order — Adjustments from Circuit 1[/h2][p align="start"]The map pool stays the same as Circuit 1 — Erangel, Miramar, Taego, and Rondo — but the order per stage has changed.[/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=",,,,,"][tr][th][p]Stage[/p][/th][th][p]Match 1[/p][/th][th][p]Match 2[/p][/th][th][p]Match 3[/p][/th][th][p]Match 4[/p][/th][th][p]Match 5[/p][/th][/tr][tr][td][p]Group Stage (PGS 4)[/p][/td][td][p]Erangel[/p][/td][td][p]Miramar[/p][/td][td][p]Taego[/p][/td][td][p]—[/p][/td][td][p]—[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]Winners / Survival / Final D1 / Grand Finals D1·D3[/p][/td][td][p]Erangel[/p][/td][td][p]Miramar[/p][/td][td][p]Taego[/p][/td][td][p]Rondo[/p][/td][td][p]Erangel[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]Final D2 / Grand Finals D2[/p][/td][td][p]Taego[/p][/td][td][p]Erangel[/p][/td][td][p]Rondo[/p][/td][td][p]Miramar[/p][/td][td][p]Taego[/p][/td][/tr][/table][p align="start"][i]*Group Stage runs the same Erangel → Miramar → Taego cycle across all three matchup rounds (A&B, B&C, A&C) for Matches 1 through 9.[/i][/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"]Key changes from Circuit 1:[/p][list][*][p]Taego comes in earlier. With Taego in the rotation from the opening matches, team map preferences and prep priorities will shift.[/p][/*][*][p]Final Stage and Grand Finals Day 2 have been fully restructured. Different late-game decisive maps mean match flow is harder to read than it was in Circuit 1.[/p][/*][/list][p align="start"] [/p][h2]Why Circuit 2 Matters — The Final Battle for EWC Qualification[/h2][p align="start"]Circuit 2's results go beyond the PGS race — they directly determine Esports World Cup (EWC) 2026 qualification.[/p][list][*][p]EWC Qualification — The top 9 teams in cumulative PGS Points from PGS 1-6 earn EWC spots. (2025 EWC champions Twisted Minds hold a separate seed.)[/p][/*][*][p]Circuit 2 is the final stage of the first half — Circuits 3 and 4 run in the second half (August onward), which means EWC qualification locks in the moment Circuit 2 ends.[/p][/*][*][p]The annual PGS Points race continues — Circuit 2 results are also a key foundation for direct qualification to PGC 2026 (top 8 teams).[/p][/*][/list][p align="start"]For teams holding a Points lead from Circuit 1, Circuit 2 is about defending that position. For the teams chasing, it's a chance to flip the standings. Three weeks from now, the first-half PGS standings are final.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][h2]PGS 6 — Where Points Count Double[/h2][p align="start"]PGS 6 is just another series in Circuit 2, but the scale of PGS Points awarded is different.[/p][list][*][p]Points go to the top 16 teams per series. Teams finishing 17th–24th earn none.[/p][/*][*][p]PGS 4 and PGS 5 award the same points (e.g., 1st = 30 pts each).[/p][/*][*][p]PGS 6 awards double (e.g., 1st = 60 pts). The Series Final week is one of the most important weeks in the PGC race.[/p][/*][/list][p align="start"]As the centerpiece of the first-half PGC/EWC race, PGS 6 carries the most weight for Circuit 2's final standings and the annual PGS Points race.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][h2]How to Watch[/h2][p align="start"]All PGS 4-6 matches are broadcast live from 19:00 KST daily on official PUBG Esports channels.[/p][p align="start"]*PGS 4 Day 1 Group Stage begins at 14:00 KST.[/p][list][*][p]PUBG Esports Twitch[/p][/*][*][p]PUBG Esports YouTube[/p][/*][*][p]Regional broadcast partners and co-streamers[/p][/*][/list][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"]The 24 teams behind Circuit 1's unpredictable drama are back — new Group Stage draw, new in-game update, same stakes. The final battle for EWC qualification starts Wednesday, May 20. See you there![/p]

[p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27971017/3ff442e156d52480a18699edb94388c0505cc174.png"][/img][/p][p]Following a dramatic Playoffs 1 weekend, we’re gearing up for the first set of PAS1 Finals! Here’s what you need to know about the schedule, format, who’s competing and more. [/p][p align="center"]Finals 1 Participants[/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=",,,"][tr][td][p align="center"]Copenhagen Wolves[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]FURIA[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Athletes of Christ[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]ROC Esports[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p align="center"]Team Falcons[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]TOYO[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Bestia[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Team Liquid[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p align="center"]No Way[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]+55 E-sports[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Newgen Allstars[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Affinity[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p align="center"]EUFAREIX10[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Pest Control[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]DUEL[/p][/td][td][p align="center"]Rent Free[/p][/td][/tr][/table][p]
[/p][h3]Twitch Drops[/h3][p]The pro players won’t be the only ones who’ll be earning a prize this weekend - you can also score some in-game items just by watching the PAS1 Finals on Twitch! (You can also snag these during the PUBG EMEA Championship strings, which take place about an hour or two before PAS each day)[/p][p]
[/p][p][b]April 24[/b][/p][list][*][p]Watch 60 minutes of the stream: Yeet! (Spray)[/p][/*][*][p]Watch 120 minutes of the stream: Casper The Caster (Emblem)[/p][/*][/list][p]
[/p][p][b]April 25[/b][/p][list][*][p]Watch 60 minutes of the stream: Victory Dance 93[/p][/*][*][p]Watch 120 minutes of the stream: Festive Flurry Jeans[/p][/*][/list][p]
[/p][p][b]April 26[/b][/p][list][*][p]Watch 30 minutes of the stream: Victory Dance 74[/p][/*][*][p]Watch 60 minutes of the stream: Festive Flurry Shoes[/p][/*][*][p]Watch 120 minutes of the stream: Festive Flurry Sweater[/p][/*][/list][p]
[/p][p]Drops will be active on [url="https://www.twitch.tv/pubg_battlegrounds"][u]PUBG: Battlegrounds (EN)[/u][/url], [url="https://www.twitch.tv/pubg_br"][u]PUBG: Battlegrounds (PTBR)[/u][/url][/p][p]
[/p][h3]What’s the format?[/h3][p]The PAS1 Finals format is tried and tested - 16 teams will face off over three days, for a total of 15 matches. Whoever has the most points at the end of play on Sunday will be crowned the Finals 1 Champion! [/p][p]
[/p][p]
[/p][h3]What’s at stake?[/h3][p]The PAS1 Finals are vitally important to any team who wants to compete on the global stage. To start with, the top 2 teams qualify directly to all PUBG Global Series events in the second half of the year (meaning PGS Circuit 2 and 3). [/p][p]Furthermore, PAS1 Finals will be the main events at which Americas teams earn PGC Points, which are used to qualify for the crown jewel of the PUBG Esports year - the PUBG Global Championship. Teams have already had an opportunity to pick up some PGC Points during the Playoffs, but the amount up for grabs is much bigger in the Finals.[/p][p]And last but certainly not least - there is $29,500 of prize money to be earned in each Finals weekend![/p][p]
[/p][h3]Wait… there’s two sets of Finals?[/h3][p]This edition of PAS1 is unique because there are [b]two[/b] sets of Playoffs and Finals. So, once this weekend’s Finals are over, we’ll be going back to the Playoffs stage next weekend with [b]Playoffs 2[/b] - where all 29 teams will start from scratch and try to qualify for Finals 2.[/p][p]

[/p][p]Be sure to tune in on our [url="https://www.twitch.tv/pubg_battlegrounds"][u]Twitch[/u][/url], [url="https://www.youtube.com/@PUBGEsports"][u]YouTube[/u][/url] and [url="https://kick.com/pubgesports"][u]Kick[/u][/url] channels to catch all of the action![/p][p]

newsitems.author: Eoin
newsitems.contents:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27971017/60395954cdf1e1477324307bf77537b9be800c17.png[/img]
Hello, PUBG Esports Fans!

The PUBG Nations Cup 2026 (PNC 2026) is returning to Seoul, South Korea, this summer!


24 teams will once again battle across five days of intense competition. With new challenger teams joining the fray, this year's PNC will feature the most diverse lineup in the tournament's history. Get ready for the ultimate all-star showdown in PUBG Esports — PUBG Nations Cup 2026!

[h3]When and Where?[/h3]

PNC 2026 will take place from June 23 to June 28, with the Grand Finals held at Jangchung Arena in Seoul — returning to the venue for the first time in seven years since 2019!

[list]
[*] Survival Stage: June 23 – 24
[*] Grand Finals: June 26 – 28
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27971017/330911f507f51193afc2018aa931fcc5ccd7780d.png[/img]

[h3]PNC 2026 Participating Teams[/h3]

24 teams will compete in this year's tournament.

[list]
[*] Defending Champion: Vietnam
[*] Argentina, Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, Chinese Taipei, Denmark, Finland, Germany, India, Indonesia, Japan, Kazakhstan, Malaysia, Neutral Team, Norway, Philippines, South Korea, Thailand, Türkiye, Ukraine, United Kingdom, United States of America
[/list]

[i][h3]New Challengers Join the Stage![/h3][/i]

Kazakhstan and Ukraine will make their PUBG Nations Cup debut at PNC 2026! Finland also makes a long-awaited return, last competing at PNC 2022. With new rosters and fresh storylines entering the mix, we can't wait to see how they'll stack up against the established powerhouses!

More details on PNC 2026 — including team rosters, ticket sales, and broadcast information — will be announced through the official PUBG Esports website in the coming weeks. We look forward to seeing you at PUBG Nations Cup 2026!

newsitems.title: PGS Circuit 1: Meta & Statistics Deepdive
newsitems.author: Eoin
newsitems.contents:
[p]Hello, PUBG Esports Fans![/p][p align="start"]From PGS 1 to PGS 3, the first circuit of the 2026 PUBG Global Series has come to a close. With a different champion crowned in every series, the competition was anything but predictable — but what choices were the pros making behind the scenes?[/p][p align="start"]In the end, survival and victory come down to the details. Which guns they ran, which items they used, how they played. Find out in the Esports Data Report: PGS Circuit 1, live now![/p][p][/p][p][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260420/JLklsRF9.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Gun Play: The AUG Era Continues[/b][/h3][p align="start"]The pros made their preference clear. The AUG dominated the AR slot with a 62.5% equip rate — up from 60.2% at PGC 2025, and pulling even further ahead of the pack. With a 44%p gap over the second-place M416 (18.2%), the AUG's place in the pro meta shows no signs of shifting.[/p][p align="start"]In the DMR/SR category, there were signs of change. The MK12 held onto first place at 45.4%, but that's a drop of over 8%p from PGC 2025 (53.6%). The Mini14 stepped into the gap, climbing from 31.5% to 37.5%. SR usage within the DMR/SR category also rose from 4.1% to 5.8% — with DNS_DIEL leading the SR kill charts at 8 kills, followed by AL_Himass and AL_Destroyy tied at 6 kills each. Whether this trend continues into Circuit 2 or gives way to something new remains to be seen.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260420/286KIc10.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Tactical Equipment: Throw It, Block It, Hide in It[/b][/h3][p align="start"]17Gaming averaged 8.55 grenades per match — by far the highest in the field. Throwing nearly 9 grenades a game isn't just aggression, it's a philosophy. Their Molotov Cocktail usage (1.43 per match) also ranked first. When 17Gaming shows up, expect something to come flying your way.[/p][p align="start"]DN SOOPers took a different approach. Top rankings in both Flashbang (2.96 per match) and Smoke Grenade (11.8 per match) usage tell a clear story: control the vision, control the game. Their playstyle is written right there in the numbers.[/p][p align="start"]Blue Zone Grenade, Emergency Cover Flare — teams across the board found ways to make every piece of tactical equipment count.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260420/T0cGBB31.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Mortar & Panzerfaust: No Longer Optional[/b][/h3][p align="start"]New equipment that felt experimental at PGC 2025 has become a staple in Circuit 1.[/p][p align="start"]Mortar usage more than doubled from 249 to 587 total fires, with hit rate climbing from 16.5% to 18.9%. The pros have moved well past the "trying it out" phase — this is tactical integration. The top Mortar kill count belongs to 17Gaming's tiantianhaovo with 7 kills.[/p][p align="start"]The Panzerfaust told an even more dramatic story. Hit rate jumped from 50.7% to 59.5%, a nearly 9% increase. DN SOOPers' DIEL led all players with 4 Panzerfaust kills — proof that this weapon is now a genuine game-changer in the right hands.[/p][p align="start"]
[img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260420/q8VqPUBk.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]PGS Moments: Who Got Got?[/b][/h3][p align="start"]11 players were taken out by BRDMs over the course of Circuit 1. 17Gaming's xwudd accounted for two of those — alone. We can only imagine what his teammates were thinking.[/p][p align="start"]Three players were knocked out by Emergency Cover: 17_tiantianhaovo, VIT_QWZYYY, and DNS_Heaven. Survival isn't just about the enemy — sometimes it's what's around you. Always stay alert![/p][p align="start"]CR_Pio, TE_Clories, TE_TanVuu, PeRo_Cui711, and FUR_zkraken all tied at the top of the Recall leaderboard with 4 each. They kept coming back. Their teammates must have been pretty busy making that happen.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260420/K2biRllO.png"][/img][/p][h3][b]Circuit 1 Final Records[/b][/h3][p align="start"]Three series, three champions. Petrichor Road took PGS 1 (95pts), Natus Vincere won PGS 2 (93pts), and Virtus.pro closed out the circuit with a dominant PGS 3 victory (136pts).[/p][p align="start"]One name kept appearing in the individual records: NAVI_Hakatory. Most kills (92) and most damage (19,590) — both. If the data had to pick the most dangerous player of Circuit 1, it wouldn't hesitate.[/p][p align="start"]Most Chicken Dinners went to Natus Vincere with 7. And the longest kill of the circuit belonged to VIT_Lev4nte at 831m — the shot that took down NAVI_boost1k- during Match 5 of the PGS 2 Survival Stage. [/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"]What will the meta look like in Circuit 2?
Stay tuned for the next Esports Data Report: PGS Circuit 2![/p]

newsitems.title: PGS 3: Virtus.pro Caps Off the First Circuit
newsitems.author: Eoin
newsitems.contents: [p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/27971017/50af079e80998745ada6e7669f4389d7149df649.png"][/img][/p][p]From PGS 1 to PGS 3, the three-week journey of the first PGS circuit, where 24 teams battled fiercely, has come to an end.[/p][p align="start"]In the PGS 3 Grand Final, which brought the circuit to a dramatic close, Virtus.pro  claimed the championship with a dominant performance of 89 kills and 136 total points.[/p][p align="start"]This circuit delivered an unpredictable storyline, with the balance of power shifting in every series. PGS 1 champion Petrichor Road, PGS 2 champion Natus Vincere, and now PGS 3 champion Virtus.pro . The fact that three different teams claimed the title across all three series highlights just how fierce the competition was throughout this circuit.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][h2][b]PGS 3 Recap[/b][/h2][h3][b]Survival Stage[/b][/h3][p align="start"]The bottom 16 teams in the cumulative PGS Points standings played five matches for a place in the Grand Final.[/p][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260409/mBzGNfjC.jpg"][/img][/p][p align="start"]eArena secured its Grand Final berth by finishing first in the Survival Stage with 48 points (26 placement + 22 kills). TEAM LIQUID placed second with 46 points after earning back-to-back Chicken Dinners in Match 2 and Match 3, while Virtus.pro  followed in third with 43 points.[/p][p align="start"]The bottom eight teams — Gen.G Esports, The Expendables, FURIA, Finhay Cerberus, Change The Game, FULL SENSE, Team Falcons, and S2G Esports — were eliminated from PGS Circuit 1.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][h3][b]Grand Final[/b][/h3][p align="start"]The top eight teams in PGS Points and the top eight teams from the Survival Stage, for a total of 16 teams, competed across 15 matches over three days to determine the PGS 3 champion.[/p][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260409/6FkXmrQS.jpg"][/img][/p][p align="start"]Virtus.pro  became the PGS 3 champion with 136 points (47 placement + 89 kills), finishing a massive 35 points ahead of second-place eArena (101 points). It was a result few could have predicted, as Virtus.pro  had been eliminated in both PGS 1 and PGS 2 and had not earned a single PGS Point before PGS 3. Their 89 kills ranked first overall in the Grand Final, and with 47 placement points added on top, they proved their strength in both firepower and survivability.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"]eArena continued its momentum from the Survival Stage, where it finished first, by taking second place in the Grand Final with 101 points, marking one of the most dramatic rises of Circuit 1. T1 finished third with 93 points, powered by an impressive 68 kills, while Crazy Raccoon climbed seven places to finish fifth with 91 points. PGS 2 champion Natus Vincere ended the event in sixth place with 90 points, but still showed its resilience by securing first place in the overall Circuit 1 PGS Points standings.[/p][p align="start"] [img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260409/PQVFn2kK.jpg"][/img][/p][p align="start"]Virtus.pro ’s Nixzyee was named the PGS 3 Grand Final MVP. Nixzyee led his team to victory with 33 kills, 4,716 damage, and 26 knockdowns in the Grand Final. The MVP also receives an individual prize of $10,000.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][h2][b]Final PGS Points Standings — PGS Circuit 1 Combined[/b][/h2][h2][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260409/j1KEQrUm.jpg"][/img][/h2][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260409/QtXuItsU.jpg"][/img][/p][p align="start"]The PGS Points from all three series have now been finalized. These points will count toward the annual PGS Points standings and will have a direct impact on qualification for the Esports World Cup (EWC) and direct qualification for the PUBG Global Championship (PGC).[/p][p align="start"] [/p][h2][b]Team Highlights — Teams That Shined in Circuit 1[/b][/h2][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260409/8EHXbWGn.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p][p align="start"][b]Virtus.pro[/b]  — PGS 3 champion. Finished 19th in PGS 1 (eliminated), was eliminated in PGS 2, and had 0 PGS Points entering PGS 3. After advancing through the Survival Stage and reaching the Grand Final, the team delivered a dominant championship run with 89 kills and 136 points, finishing 35 points ahead of second place. Nixzyee’s MVP performance (33 kills, 4,716 damage, 26 knockdowns) perfectly symbolized the team’s PGS 3 run. Virtus.pro  also ranked first in total prize earnings for Circuit 1 with $102,000.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"][b]Natus Vincere[/b] — Finished first in cumulative PGS Points with 69 points. From sixth place in PGS 1 (13 points), to a dramatic comeback title in PGS 2 (30 points), to sixth place in the PGS 3 Grand Final (26 points), the team consistently earned points across all three series and claimed the top spot in the overall Circuit 1 points race. It was a case where consistency at the top mattered more than a single explosive result.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260409/s0Qd1NRx.jpg"][/img][/p][p align="start"][b]eArena[/b] — The team that showed the most dramatic growth curve in Circuit 1. After finishing 16th in PGS 1 (1 point) and remaining in the lower ranks in PGS 2 (4 points), eArena surged to first place in the PGS 3 Survival Stage and then second place in the Grand Final (101 points), achieving its best result of the tournament. The team finished fifth overall in Circuit 1 with 53 points and earned a total of $52,000, emerging as a new powerhouse from the APAC region.[/p][p align="start"] [img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260409/vdgqdTDV.jpg"][/img][/p][p align="start"][b]Crazy Raccoon[/b] — Like eArena, Crazy Raccoon was one of the breakout teams of PGS 3. After being eliminated in PGS 1 (0 points) and finishing 15th in PGS 2 (1 point), the team had little presence in the earlier stages of the circuit. But in the PGS 3 Grand Final, it climbed seven places to finish fifth with 91 points and 30 PGS Points. That single-event performance brought the team to 11th place overall with 31 points.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260409/dAfyX0XF.jpg"][/img][/p][p align="start"][b]T1[/b] — A team that best illustrated the benefits of the circuit structure. T1 finished fifth in PGS 1 with 15 points, but was eliminated in PGS 2 and earned no points there. Even so, its PGS 1 points were enough to send the team directly to the PGS 3 Grand Final, where it secured third place with 93 points and 40 PGS Points, finishing Circuit 1 in fourth overall with 55 points.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260409/PZ7pmkrq.jpg"][/img][/p][p align="start"][b]Petrichor Road[/b] — PGS 1 champion (30 points) and second in the overall Circuit 1 PGS Points standings with 68 points. Although the team’s placement declined over the course of the series (PGS 1: 1st → PGS 2: 3rd → PGS 3: 8th), its steady point accumulation across all three events stood out. The points built up in PGS 1 and PGS 2 ultimately carried Petrichor Road to second place overall in Circuit 1.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"] [/p][h2][b]Player of the Day — PGS 3[/b][/h2][p][/p][p align="start"][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260409/qwMV2Khv.jpg"][/img][/p][p align="start"][/p][p align="start"]By fan vote, the Player of the Day for PGS 3 is MMing from Petrichor Road![/p][p align="start"] [img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260409/82jD9nRO.jpg"][/img][/p][p][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260409/8ka5YBaf.png"][/img][/p][p align="start"] [/p][h1][b]Circuit 1 Total Prize Pool[/b][/h1][p align="start"]The $500,000 total prize pool for Circuit 1 (PGS 1–3) has now been fully distributed![/p][p align="start"] [img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260409/0ew50G8i.jpg"][/img][img src="https://wstatic-prod-boc.krafton.com/common/news/20260409/WMz7PN6L.jpg"][/img][/p][h1][/h1][h1][b]Looking Back on Circuit 1[/b][/h1][p align="start"]Three weeks of Circuit 1 showed what the new circuit format can produce.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"]Three series, three different champions — Petrichor Road (PGS 1), Natus Vincere (PGS 2), Virtus.pro  (PGS 3). The top of the standings changed every single week.[/p][p align="start"]PGS 3 comebacks — Virtus.pro  went from 0 PGS Points through PGS 1–2 to PGS 3 Champion, while eArena and Crazy Raccoon surged from the bottom half into the upper ranks.[/p][p align="start"]The power of cumulative points — PGS Points leader Natus Vincere (69 pts) earned their position not from a single dominant series, but through consistent results across all three. T1's PGS 1 points alone carried them into the PGS 3 Grand Finals — proof that the circuit structure rewards sustained performance.[/p][p align="start"] [/p][p align="start"]Thank you to every fan who followed along for the past three weeks. The second circuit of the PUBG Global Series returns in May. The 2026 season is just getting started — with three more circuits, Regional Series, the Esports World Cup, and the PUBG Global Championship still to come, the PUBG Esports journey continues![/p]
